speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment since the introduction of the guidelines for the usage of light emitting wreaths and inflatables at funeral wakes in June 2022 (a) how many complaints have been received relating to the flouting of the guidelines; (b) what have been the challenges of enforcing the guidelines; and (c) whether there will be a further review of the guidelines should concerns persist.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: When such feedback is received, the respective Town Councils and land agencies would be notified to engage the relevant parties to address these concerns.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Understandably, of course, wakes are sensitive and emotional times for families.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Therefore, also makes it difficult for agencies to enforce the guidelines, even with as much tact that is available, much less to remove the wreaths if they are any contraventions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is also difficult for bereaved families to be able to advise well wishes not to send such wreaths beyond the advised number.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Affected residents also understandably lean on agencies, such as the Town Council, to enforce what are advisories.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Indeed, the light-emitting wreaths are a more recent Innovation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But the display of wreaths at wakes are part of a cultural tradition.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, there are people who even think that using light-emitting wreaths are more sustainable because they can be reused and do not contribute to waste as compared to other traditional wreaths.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But what is important is how are these light-emitting wreaths being used, whether they are placed and used in a responsible manner.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, the Town Councils land agencies are responsible to ensure adherence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But I note the Member's point that during bereavement, there needs to be a bit more sensitivity to enforce such guidelines.
